hypothesis: A learned graded terminal-score preference improves low-visit policy improvement and endgame behavior where win/loss estimates provide little distinction. Prior long games motivate this test but do not establish the cause.
intervention: Both arms train an additional E[(2/pi)*atan(current_player_margin/(2*board_size))] head by MSE at weight1.0, retaining ownership weight1.5 and separate true win/loss targets. Control utility factor0; candidate factor0.3. Normalize neural and terminal utilities, PUCT exploration and FPU reduction by1+factor. No other configured training choice differs.
control: Fresh factor-zero training, not reused historical weights. Identical full initial parameter tree in both arms.
primary_metric: Separate paired-color outcomes and incomplete games against pinned official9x9 KataGo at1 and16 visits, candidate16 simulations, openings[] and[C3,G7], cap324 moves and360 seconds/game. Eight games per arm, exploratory screen only.
secondary_metrics: training wall time and CPU time
root visit support and predicted score-value calibration diagnostics
promotion: No superiority, equivalence or sample-efficiency claim from an observed zero-win floor or incomplete paired panel. A promising result needs fresh training seeds and larger complete external panels. No production promotion from this pilot.
limitations: Score utility is a component control, not full KataGo reproduction.
The head learns expected bounded score directly, rather than KataGo score-distribution and dynamic utility machinery.
One initialization; actual update counts can differ with replay warmup.
Do not equate more terminal rows or lower self-play losses with stronger play.
Both configured utility and the implied exploration normalization are part of the intervention.
lineage: From scratch. Official KataGo weights and evaluation records do not enter training.
